When a customer receives a message that says their order has shipped with Blue Dart, Delhivery or another courier, what they want to know is simple: where is my parcel, when will it arrive, and what do I do if something goes wrong? An online store should answer all three on its own website, through an order tracking page and well-timed shipment updates, rather than sending customers off to a courier's site with an unfamiliar AWB number and a status code they have to decode. This guide explains how to build that properly: what the tracking page should show, how to translate courier statuses into plain language, how to send updates by email, SMS and WhatsApp, and how to handle delays and failed deliveries, so that "where is my order?" messages stop filling your inbox.

It is written for store owners and the developers who build Shopify, WooCommerce and custom stores. It is about the website and messaging side only; choosing a courier or negotiating rates is a separate decision.

## Why "what does Blue Dart mean for my order?" is a website problem

Many shoppers do not know or care which courier carries their parcel. When the shipping email says "Shipped via Blue Dart, AWB 12345678901", some customers are reassured, but many are confused: is Blue Dart the seller? Do I need to contact them? Why does the courier site say "In transit — hub scan" for three days?

Every one of those questions becomes a message to your team. "Where is my order?" queries are among the most common customer service contacts for online stores, and they arrive at the worst times: during sales, festivals and bad weather. Most of them can be prevented by the website telling customers, clearly and proactively, what is happening.

The aim is that customers see your brand at every step, understand the status in plain words, know what to expect next and know exactly how to get help.

## The order tracking page

A tracking page on your own domain, such as `yourstore.com/track/`, is the centre of the system. Customers reach it from links in shipping messages, from their account's order history, and from a "Track order" link in the header or footer.

### How customers look up an order

Offer two routes:

- **From a link in an email, SMS or WhatsApp message**, which opens the page for that order directly using a secure token in the URL, without a login.
- **From a lookup form**, where the customer enters the order number plus the email address or phone number used at checkout.

Do not allow lookup by order number alone. Sequential order numbers are easy to guess, and a page showing names, addresses and items to anyone who types a number is a privacy problem. Under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, you are responsible for protecting customers' personal data with reasonable security safeguards. Show the minimum needed: partial address (area and pincode, not the full street address) is usually enough on the tracking page itself.

### What the page should show

In order of importance:

1. **Current status in plain language**, prominently: "On its way — expected Thursday 14 November"
2. **Expected delivery date or window**, updated if it changes
3. **A simple progress bar** with stages: Order confirmed → Packed → Shipped → Out for delivery → Delivered
4. **Items in the shipment**, with images, especially if an order is split into several parcels
5. **The courier name and AWB number**, with a link to the courier's own tracking page for customers who want the full scan history
6. **A timeline of events**, translated into plain language, with the raw courier status available on tap for those who want it
7. **What to do if there is a problem**: a clear help link, WhatsApp button or contact form pre-filled with the order number
8. **Delivery address area and pincode**, so customers can spot an error early

If an order has several shipments, show each one as a separate card with its own status and courier.

### Mobile first

Most customers open tracking links from a phone, often from WhatsApp or SMS. The page must load quickly on mobile data, show the status without scrolling and keep buttons large enough to tap easily. Avoid heavy scripts, sliders and pop-ups on this page.

### Use the page to help, not to sell

It is reasonable to show a small "You may also like" section or a referral offer below the tracking details, but keep it below the status and help sections. A customer anxious about a late parcel will not appreciate a sale banner pushing the status out of view.

## Translating courier statuses into plain language

Courier tracking data is written for logistics operators. Status codes and scan descriptions such as "Shipment arrived at hub", "Undelivered — consignee not available" or "RTO initiated" mean little to most customers, and each courier uses different wording.

Build a mapping table that converts every status your couriers send into one of a small number of customer-facing stages, with a customer-friendly message. Illustrative example:

| Courier status (example) | Customer stage | Message shown |
|---|---|---|
| Manifested / pickup scheduled | Packed | "Packed and waiting for the courier to collect it" |
| Picked up / in transit / hub scans | Shipped | "On its way. Expected by [date]" |
| Out for delivery | Out for delivery | "Out for delivery today. Keep your phone handy" |
| Delivered | Delivered | "Delivered on [date]. Not received? Tell us here" |
| Undelivered — customer not available | Delivery attempt failed | "The courier could not deliver today. They will try again; or update your details here" |
| Address issue | Action needed | "The courier needs help finding your address. Please confirm it here" |
| Return to origin initiated | Returning to us | "Your parcel is being returned to us. We will contact you" |

Keep the raw status available behind a "Show courier details" toggle. It is useful for your support team and for customers who prefer detail.

Review the mapping when you add a courier or aggregator, and log any status your system does not recognise so a developer can add it. Unmapped statuses are a common reason tracking pages show nonsense.

## Getting tracking data into your store

### Platform options

- **Shopify** provides an order status page and shipping notifications, and supports adding tracking numbers and courier links to fulfilments. Shipping apps and aggregator integrations can update tracking automatically. A branded tracking page usually comes from an app or a custom theme section.
- **WooCommerce** does not include tracking by default. Extensions such as WooCommerce Shipment Tracking, or aggregator plugins, add tracking numbers to orders and emails. A custom tracking page is usually built as a template using the order data.
- **Custom stores** integrate with courier or aggregator APIs directly.

### Webhooks over polling

Wherever possible, receive status updates by webhook (the courier or aggregator notifies your system when something changes) rather than repeatedly checking the courier's API. Webhooks are faster, reduce API usage and let you trigger messages at the right moment. Keep a scheduled check as a fallback for shipments that have not updated in a while.

### Store the history

Save each status event with its timestamp in your database, rather than fetching live from the courier every time a customer opens the page. This makes the page faster, keeps working if a courier's API is slow, and gives your team a record for resolving disputes.

## Shipment notifications: email, SMS and WhatsApp

Notifications should tell customers what they need to know before they think to ask. A sensible set:

1. **Order confirmed** (immediately after purchase)
2. **Shipped**, with expected delivery date and tracking link
3. **Out for delivery**
4. **Delivered**, with a link to report a problem
5. **Exceptions**: delay, failed attempt, address issue, return to origin

Avoid sending a message for every hub scan. Too many messages train customers to ignore them.

### Email

Every store should send transactional emails for these events. Keep them short, put the status and the tracking button at the top, and send from a domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up so they reach the inbox. Our guide to [order confirmation pages and transactional emails](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-order-confirmation-page-transactional-emails-2026) covers templates and deliverability.

### SMS

Transactional SMS in India must be sent through a registered sender ID with templates approved on a DLT platform under TRAI's rules. Keep SMS for the most important events (shipped, out for delivery, exceptions) and include the short tracking link.

### WhatsApp

Many Indian customers prefer WhatsApp. Order and shipping updates can be sent through the WhatsApp Business Platform using utility templates approved by Meta. Customers must have opted in to receive WhatsApp messages from you, typically with a clear checkbox at checkout. Meta charges per delivered template message, and rates vary by category and country, so check current pricing with your provider before rolling out messages for every stage. A useful pattern is to send "Shipped" and "Out for delivery" on WhatsApp, with a "Need help?" button that opens a conversation with your support team or a bot that can answer status questions. Our guide to [WhatsApp order update messages](/blog/whatsapp-order-updates-api-india) explains template setup.

### Consistent links

Every notification should link to your own tracking page, not straight to the courier's site. That keeps the customer in your store's experience, lets you show the plain-language status and help options, and gives you data on how often customers check.

## Handling delays and failed deliveries

The real test of a tracking system is what happens when things go wrong.

### Delays

If a shipment has not moved for longer than usual for its route, or has passed its expected date, update the expected date on the tracking page and tell the customer before they ask: "Your parcel is delayed by the courier. New expected date: Saturday. We are keeping an eye on it." A proactive delay message turns a complaint into a moment of trust.

Set up an internal alert for shipments that are stuck so your team can contact the courier.

### Failed delivery attempts

When a courier reports an unsuccessful attempt, send an exception message that explains what happened and offers a simple action: confirm the phone number, add a landmark, choose a preferred time if the courier supports it, or contact support. A short form on the tracking page that updates the address details and alerts your team can prevent a return to origin.

### Address problems

Many delivery failures start at checkout with incomplete addresses. Good checkout design, with pincode lookup, a landmark field and phone validation, prevents a large share of them. Our guide to [showing delivery estimates, courier options and order tracking](/blog/blue-dart-vs-delhivery-which-is-faster-2026) covers the checkout side, including pincode serviceability checks.

### Returns to origin

If a parcel is returning to you, tell the customer, explain what happens next (refund, reshipment or contact from your team) and make it easy to respond. Silence is what turns these cases into chargebacks and bad reviews.

## Measuring whether it works

| Measure | Where | Good sign |
|---|---|---|
| "Where is my order?" contacts per 100 orders | Support inbox, WhatsApp, calls | Falls after launch |
| Tracking page visits per order | GA4 | Customers self-serve rather than asking |
| Help clicks from the tracking page | GA4 events | Problems reach support with the order number attached |
| Failed delivery attempts converted to deliveries | Order data | Rises after exception messages are added |
| Message delivery and read rates | Email, SMS and WhatsApp provider reports | Messages reach customers |

Measure the contact rate for a month before the new tracking page goes live, so you have a baseline.

## A build checklist

- [ ] Tracking page on your own domain, linked from header or footer and account pages
- [ ] Lookup requires order number plus email or phone; links in messages use secure tokens
- [ ] Only necessary personal details shown
- [ ] Plain-language status, expected date and progress bar at the top
- [ ] Split shipments shown separately
- [ ] Courier status mapping covers every status from every courier, with unmapped statuses logged
- [ ] Status updates received by webhook and stored with timestamps
- [ ] Notifications for confirmed, shipped, out for delivery, delivered and exceptions
- [ ] SMS templates registered on DLT; WhatsApp templates approved and customers opted in
- [ ] Delay and failed-attempt messages with a clear action
- [ ] Help button that carries the order number
- [ ] GA4 events on tracking views and help clicks

## What it costs

Indicative effort, depending on platform and number of couriers:

- **Shopify with an existing tracking app:** setup, branding, status mapping and notification templates typically take a few days.
- **WooCommerce with an extension or aggregator plugin plus a custom tracking page:** typically one to two weeks including testing.
- **Custom integration with courier or aggregator APIs, webhooks and multi-channel notifications:** more, depending on the number of couriers and channels.

Ongoing costs include any app or plugin subscription, SMS charges and WhatsApp message charges.

## Frequently asked questions

### Should my online store have its own order tracking page?
Yes. A tracking page on your own domain keeps customers in your store's experience, shows status in plain language instead of courier codes, offers help with the order number attached and reduces "where is my order?" messages.

### Why does the courier tracking show "in transit" for days?
Parcels can sit between hub scans for a day or more on longer routes, and some couriers update only at major hubs. Show the expected delivery date prominently, and alert your team when a shipment has not moved for longer than is normal for its route so you can follow up.

### Can I send order updates on WhatsApp?
Yes, through the WhatsApp Business Platform using Meta-approved utility templates, to customers who have opted in. Meta charges per delivered template message, so many stores reserve WhatsApp for key events such as shipped and out for delivery.

### How do I stop customers seeing other people's orders on the tracking page?
Require the order number plus the email or phone number used at checkout, use secure, hard-to-guess tokens in tracking links, and show only partial address details. Do not allow lookup by order number alone.

### Do I need DLT registration for shipping SMS in India?
Yes. Commercial and transactional SMS in India must be sent with a registered sender ID and templates registered on a DLT platform under TRAI's regulations. Your SMS provider can guide you through registration.
